## Second CMS Deployment Test

This is a second publishing test for the portfolio CMS. The purpose of this post is to confirm that newly created content can move through the complete publishing process without requiring a manual Git push or production redeployment.


![photo](/uploads/photo.jpg "zdxfcdf")


After this article is published, the CMS should update the blog content stored in GitHub and trigger a new Vercel production deployment automatically.

### Testing the New Publishing Flow

The publishing process should begin when the Publish Blog Post button is clicked in the admin dashboard.


![gig image](/uploads/gig image-9.jpg "zsxcdsad")


The CMS should first save this article to the GitHub repository. After the GitHub update completes, the server should trigger the configured Vercel Deploy Hook.

### Expected GitHub Update

- A new entry for this article should be added to the blog JSON file in the repository.
- The title, slug, article content, featured image, metadata, and other information should remain available after refreshing the CMS.

### Expected Vercel Deployment

1. Once the GitHub update is successful, the CMS should request a new production deployment from Vercel.
2. A new deployment should appear in the Vercel dashboard without requiring any terminal command.


![b&w image](/uploads/b&w image-2.png "sdcsdf")


### Live Website Test

After the Vercel deployment reaches the Ready state, this post should appear on the main blog page.

The individual article URL should also load correctly using the slug assigned to this post.

### Deployment Status Test

The CMS should provide a clear status message after publishing.

*If everything works correctly, the admin dashboard should confirm that the GitHub content was updated and the Vercel production deployment was triggered.*

### Final Verification

This article is temporary and is being used only to test the automatic CMS publishing workflow.

After confirming that it appears correctly on the live website, the post will be deleted from the CMS to verify that deletion also triggers a new production deployment and removes the article from the live site.

title: Testing Automatic CMS Deployment for Blog Updates
excerpt: This test post checks whether the CMS can publish content to GitHub, trigger a Vercel deployment, update the live blog, and remove the post after deletion.
author: Ahsanul Haque Chowdhury
metaTitle: Testing Automatic CMS Deployment for Blog Updates
metaDescription: A test post for checking automatic GitHub commits, Vercel deployments, live blog updates, editing, and deletion from the portfolio CMS.
content:
## Testing the CMS Publishing Workflow

[This blog post is being](https://facebook.com) published as a practical test of the content management system. The goal is to confirm that a new blog post can be created from the admin dashboard, committed automatically to GitHub, and deployed to the live website through Vercel.


![gig image](/uploads/gig image-1.jpg "sfcdsf")


> The complete workflow should happen without using manual Git commands after the CMS is properly configured.

### What This Test Should Confirm

This test should verify several important parts of the publishing process.

- The post appears in the CMS after publishing
- The blog data is updated in GitHub
- A new Vercel production deployment is triggered
- The post appears on the live blog page
- The individual blog post URL works correctly

If all of these steps work, the publishing workflow is functioning as expected.

## Testing Content Formatting


![my signature](/uploads/my signature-11.jpg "zsfcdzsf")


This section checks whether the blog renderer handles common formatting correctly.

**This sentence is bold text.**

*This sentence is italic text.*

The CMS should preserve this formatting after the post is committed and deployed.

### Testing Lists

The following bullet list is included for testing:

- Frontend development
- Technical SEO
- WordPress management
- Website performance
- Online reputation management


![signature of ahsan](/uploads/signature of ahsan-4.jpg "asdff")


The following numbered list should also display correctly:

1. Publish the post
2. Check the GitHub commit
3. Check the Vercel deployment
4. Open the live blog
5. Delete the test post

## Testing Links

A blog post may also include external links.

You can visit [Google Search Central](https://developers.google.com/search) as an example external link.

The link should remain clickable after the article is published.

### Testing a Quote

> A reliable CMS should make routine content publishing simple, repeatable, and easy to verify.

This blockquote is included to confirm that quote formatting works correctly on the individual blog page.

## Testing Automatic Deployment

- After this post is published, the CMS should update the blog JSON file in the GitHub repository.
- The publishing API should then trigger the configured Vercel Deploy Hook so that a new production deployment begins automatically.
- Once the deployment is ready, this article should appear on the live blog page without requiring a manual Git push.

### Final Delete Test

1. After confirming that this post appears correctly on the live website, the final step is to delete it from the CMS.
2. The deletion should update the GitHub blog data, trigger another Vercel production deployment, and remove this post from both the main blog page and its individual URL.

If the post disappears after the deployment completes, the full create and delete workflow is working correctly.
